set.typical_award_size: The Marin County Affordable Housing Fund (Housing Trust Fund, created 1988) is capitalized by inclusionary in-lieu fees, the single-family Affordable Housing Impact Fee, commercial linkage fees and County General Fund contributions (Guidelines 2023-2027, adopted Dec 12, 2023). It funds seed and catalyst costs, land acquisition, predevelopment, construction and gap financing; awards are generally $50,000 per unit, up to $100,000 per unit depending on funds, project type, location, bedrooms, affordability depth and restriction term, with higher amounts considered in high-resource areas. About 25% of funds are prioritized for preservation and rehab and 75% for new construction or conversion. Funds are generally loans (3 months to 55 years); the Board may award grants for smaller requests. The Fund also supplies the 1:1 local match for PLHA through the annual NOFA. The 2026-27 NOFA estimated about $3,100,000 total ($1,500,000 CDBG, $700,000 HOME, $900,000 PLHA inclusive of Trust Fund match). On June 23, 2026 the Board approved FY 2026-27 allocations: $676,641 HOME, $1,611,279 CDBG, and $476,762 estimated PLHA matched 1:1 by $476,762 from the Trust Fund (Oak Hill, Eden Housing, $553,524 combined; Bayfront Terrace, EAH, $400,000 combined); staff reported a Housing Fund balance of $14,032,062 after the match. Standalone Board actions recorded in earlier agendas include a $5,239,098 Trust Fund loan to Habitat for Humanity Greater San Francisco (April 15, 2025) and a $3,000,000 Golden Gate Village predevelopment loan restructured April 14, 2026.
set.per_unit_cap: Generally $50,000 per unit; up to $100,000 per unit in some circumstances (Affordable Housing Fund Guidelines 2023-2027).
set.affordability_requirement: Low, very low and extremely low income households; affordability restrictions in perpetuity unless the Board approves a shorter term required by a public financing source. Priorities: AFFH, leverage, high-resource areas, unincorporated Marin, RHNA, homeownership. Projects in cities and towns must waive all planning and building fees and, if the jurisdiction has a housing trust, provide a match from it.
set.cycle_notes: Two tracks. Affordable Housing Fund applications are accepted throughout the year through the Neighborly portal and go to the Board individually. PLHA plus Trust Fund match, HOME and CDBG are awarded through the annual NOFA: the 2026-27 window ran January 19 to February 19, 2026, with PSC review May 19 and Board approval June 23, 2026. The County states it opens the NOFA toward the beginning of each calendar year.
set.next_deadline: No open NOFA round as of November 8, 2026; the 2027-28 NOFA is expected to open early in calendar 2027 per the County funding page. Affordable Housing Fund requests are accepted year-round.

set.typical_award_size: Measure W (2018) made West Marin a special transient occupancy tax area with an additional 4% tax on short-term rentals, funding long-term community housing and emergency services. Under the guidelines approved by the Board on August 18, 2026 (in effect July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), Direct Housing Assistance receives $100,000 a year and Housing Production receives the remainder of the community housing funds, covering predevelopment, acquisition, development and preservation of rental and ownership housing, septic upgrades for deed-restricted units, conversions, ADUs and JADUs, and transitional housing. Recommended awards are $50,000 per affordable unit plus $20,000 per bedroom for units of two or more bedrooms at up to 80% AMI, as funds allow. Example: $210,000 Measure W plus $300,000 Affordable Housing Fund considered for CLAM's 55/65 Second Street, Point Reyes Station (April 7, 2026).
set.per_unit_cap: $50,000 per affordable unit plus $20,000 per bedroom for two-bedroom and larger units at up to 80% AMI, as funds are available (FY 2026-27 guidelines).
set.affordability_requirement: Projects in the Measure W tax area serving households up to 120% AMI are prioritized; the per-unit plus per-bedroom formula applies to units at up to 80% AMI. Eligible applicants are 501(c)(3) nonprofits and public agencies only, so a for-profit developer would need a nonprofit or public partner.
set.cycle_notes: Applications accepted on a rolling basis through the County Neighborly portal (same form as the Affordable Housing Fund). Category balances reset each July 1 and priorities are set annually by the Board on the Measure W Working Group recommendation; current guidelines run through June 30, 2027.
set.next_deadline: No deadline; rolling applications as of November 8, 2026.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Conduit tax-exempt bond financing is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b): DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, Public Works Case No. 2006-020, Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village, held that neither publicly offered nor privately placed housing revenue bonds (or federal LIHTC) trigger prevailing wage. https://www.Dir.Ca.Gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf. Other public funds in the same deal (County Trust Fund, HOME, MHA loans) are evaluated separately and can trigger prevailing wage.

set.typical_award_size: The FY 2026-27 to FY 2028-29 BHSA Integrated Plan (Board approved Dec 9, 2025; DHCS-approved version posted) programs $68,115,848 over three years. Housing Interventions receive 30% of base allocations: $5,854,517 in year one, $5,733,901 in year two and $5,695,539 in year three (plus $125,000 of unspent MHSA moved to housing). Planned uses: rental and operating subsidies at four PSH programs, 16 to 22 local Behavioral Health vouchers, continuation of transitional rent and Bridge Housing programs after they end, a peer respite facility, and capital development for a new PSH project in year one. Known capital award: up to $1,931,918 in MHSA/BHSA capital match ($1,531,918 required match plus $400,000 contingency) for the nine-unit Carmelita House Homekey+ PSH conversion (April 14, 2026), with a BHSA-funded operating agreement and services contract to follow. Scattered-site housing and rental subsidy RFP HHS-2026-02 closed April 17, 2026.
set.cycle_notes: Plan in effect July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 with annual updates. Capital is awarded project by project (Homekey+ match) and subsidies and services through County RFPs (HHS-2026-02 closed April 17, 2026), not a standing NOFA.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Watch County HHS RFP postings and the annual plan update; ask BHRS about capital match or operating subsidies for PSH units.
set.layering_notes: funding_type grant: the plan funds housing capital (forgivable capital grants such as Carmelita House) and rental and operating subsidies. Marin's BHSA housing money is about $5,700,000 to $5,900,000 a year and is being used as the local match that makes Homekey+ and small PSH conversions work, plus scattered-site rental subsidies and operating subsidies. The plan notes the Marin Housing Authority has had a voucher shortfall since August 2024, which is why BHSA is funding local vouchers. Sources: HHS BHSA page and DHCS-approved Integrated Plan PDF, April 14, 2026 Carmelita House staff report, RFP HHS-2026-02.

set.typical_award_size: No published guidelines or NOFA. The Affordable Housing Programs Fund (Fund 210) receives in-lieu fees, BMR resale and monitoring fees and interest, and mainly pays for BMR program administration, with occasional project support: past loans to Eden Housing ($1,500,000), Homeward Bound Oma Village ($600,000) and Habitat northwest quad ($427,438). For Habitat for Humanity's 80-unit Redwood Boulevard ownership project the Council granted $350,000 for development impact fees plus waivers of several City fees (March 14, 2023) and a further grant of up to $1,000,000 ($800,000 from Fund 210 plus $200,000 transferred from the General Fund) for processing fees (March 11, 2025). Staff projected a Fund 210 balance of $1,132,422 at June 30, 2025, leaving about $332,422 for other projects after reserving $650,000 for BMR buybacks, and said the fund no longer has large balances because developers build inclusionary units on site.
set.affordability_requirement: Zoning Code 19.24.040 requires in-lieu fees to go to a separate City fund for very low, low and moderate income housing; awards carry regulatory agreements set per project (Habitat: 60 low and 20 moderate income ownership units). Inclusionary requirement 10% for 7 to 10 units rising to 20% at 20 or more units (19.24.030).
set.cycle_notes: No NOFA; developers request funds directly and the Council acts by resolution. City support also satisfies the County Affordable Housing Fund local-match requirement.
set.next_deadline: No open round; requests go to Council through the Community Development Department as of November 8, 2026.
set.layering_notes: Treat as a small, negotiated gap or fee-offset source, roughly $1,000,000 per project at most and limited by a low fund balance; mainly useful to meet the Marin County Affordable Housing Fund requirement that cities waive fees and provide a local match. set.typical_award_size: 100% waiver of City application processing fees for projects managed and operated by affordable housing organizations when at least 10% of units serve very low income households (Housing Element Program 14 text) or extremely low income households (Program 23 and 2024 APR wording), adopted by ordinance and resolution in October 2022. Separately, MVMC 5.32 provides a 50% reduction in City fees, licenses and taxes for units affordable to and occupied by lower and moderate income households. Lot merger fees are waived for projects using the Opportunity Site Housing Overlay (2024 overlay ordinance). Affordable projects are also exempt from the Chapter 20.80 impact fee. Dollar value depends on the City fee schedule.
